summary: The article describes how community learning centers (CLCs) have grown since September 2023 by partnering with local businesses, nonprofits, universities and civic groups. It profiles programs such as the Lincoln Learning Hub, Madison Maker Space, Harmony Project, Forward Together, Grandview Language Institute and Horizon Tech Hub's Tech Tuesdays. It concludes that ongoing evaluation and community input keep these partnerships responsive and make education more accessible and practical.
one_line: Community learning centers are using partnerships with local businesses, nonprofits and universities to expand accessible, practical, lifelong education programs.
key_facts: The Lincoln Learning Hub in Lincolnville launched its workshops on November 1, 2023; its director is Julie Patterson.
The Madison Maker Space in downtown Elmwood broke ground on December 15, 2023, through a partnership between Elmwood School District and a collective of tech companies led by CEO Michael Torres.

The Harmony Project was launched by the Vista Community Center on September 28, 2023, with local music schools and the Green Harmony Non-Profit Organization, to give disadvantaged youth access to music.
Sarah Bennett, founder of Green Harmony, said of the Harmony Project: "It's about providing a soundtrack to education."
The Forward Together Youth Leadership Program was established at the Springfield Community Learning Center on January 20, 2024, with local universities and civic organizations.
Forward Together mentors young leaders in civic engagement and community project management; its coordinator is Thomas Reed.
The Grandview Language Institute started its community integration program on October 3, 2023, offering language sessions for both immigrants and local residents.
Amelia Rodriguez, lead coordinator of the Grandview Language Institute, said: "Language is a bridge."
The Horizon Tech Hub in Riverside began "Tech Tuesdays" on February 7, 2024, offering free workshops on topics from coding to digital marketing.
Eric Nguyen is director of the Horizon Tech Hub, and the workshops aim to help close the digital divide.
CLCs hold town-hall-style meetings so community voices are integrated into planning, and they run regular evaluations to keep programs responsive.
CLC offerings range from language classes by multilingual educators to cooking workshops led by acclaimed chefs, supporting intergenerational and multicultural learning.
